- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid over-optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% in 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ days ≤0.3), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid false breakout signals.  
- When forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3+ days, increase forecast by 1–2% per day to correct for underestimation bias.
